scope: All particles predicted. No MPM or force network at inference. Reference data use dynamic two-way MJWarp–MPM.

results.name: Reference data
results.summary: 156 training, 6 validation, and 12 reserved test episodes collected. Each episode contains 4,000 particles and 300 transitions at 5 ms. Box, sphere, and cylinder geometries; 0.02 m MPM grid; 25 MPM iterations. Additional training independently varies body mass across material sets and includes smaller bodies.

results.name: Coupled rollout comparison
results.summary: Means of episode RMS errors over completed 1.5-second rollouts. Failed runs are shown explicitly; their shorter-horizon errors are excluded. All methods except the stationary baseline predict particle motion. Peak error is the RMS vertical-force error at each reference peak time. Parameters are selected on validation episodes only.

results.name: Current validation selection
results.summary: Four-step training + static-contact correction. Selection requires all six coupled validation rollouts to complete, then compares particle, body-position, and force errors with fixed normalization scales. This is a development result, not an independent test result.

results.name: Sampled SDF geometry check
results.summary: Reference particle and body states isolate geometry error. Thirty sampled transitions per shape. At 5 mm SDF sampling, force differences from analytic geometry are 0.11–0.22 N RMS. A separate triangle-mesh SDF control is reported below.

results.name: Newton rigid-body integration
results.summary: All six validation episodes complete with learned particles and analytical forces. Mean particle error 1.42 cm, body-position error 1.76 cm, force error 5.24 N. Newton handles rigid dynamics and direct rigid contacts; it contains no MPM particles or MPM solver. Reference-force replay reproduces one box trajectory within 0.53 micrometers RMS.

results.name: Learned box simulation
results.summary: Left: reference MJWarp–MPM. Right: four-step GNN + static-contact correction + analytical reactions + Newton MJWarp. The right view uses predicted particles and body motion throughout. This validation episode still underestimates impact: peak vertical material-on-box force 98.5 N versus 145.0 N reference.

results.name: Learned cylinder simulation
results.summary: Four-step GNN with static-contact correction; dynamic Newton rigid body. All 4,000 particle positions are predicted. Peak upward material-on-body force: 73.1 N predicted, 115.2 N reference. This is a validation episode.

results.name: All-particle memory feasibility
results.summary: The 296,875-particle G1-sized bed fits in GPU memory: 9.1–9.8 million directed graph edges, 2.9–3.1 GB allocated GPU tensor memory. Every particle and edge is evaluated using bounded computation chunks. Three one-step queries only; no large-bed rollout or isolated speed comparison is established.

metrics.scope: Three one-step reference-state queries on the 296,875-particle G1-sized bed. Every particle and every local graph edge is evaluated. No region selector, force reconstruction, or coupled rollout. Concurrent training prevents a speed comparison.

results.name: Large-bed rollout: poor transfer
results.summary: All 296,875 particles and the dynamic 2 kg box advance without MPM for 100 steps (0.5 s). Particle error is 1.33 cm, box-position error 5.57 cm, and force error 45.03 N. The predicted impact occurs too late. This changes both bed size and material parameters relative to the six small-bed validation episodes, so it does not isolate the cause. This is a short development diagnostic, not a successful full-bed simulator.

metrics.scope: Development scaling diagnostic, 100 transitions / 0.5 s; all 296875 particles. Not a full-duration independent test.

results.name: Controlled large-bed comparison
results.summary: The transfer error remains when material, box mass, and initial box state match small-bed validation. With recorded particles, the freely integrated box has 0.49 cm position error and 11.63 N force error. With learned particles, those errors rise to 5.72 cm and 24.88 N. The initial top particle layer is 2.68 cm too low on average at 0.5 s. This implicates particle-motion transfer in the additional error; the analytical estimator still has its own impact error.

learned.scope: Development scaling diagnostic, 100 transitions / 0.5 s; all 296875 particles. Not a full-duration independent test.

recorded_particle_control.scope: Reference particles retained, freely integrated Newton box; material and initial body state match the learned large-bed diagnostic. No particle learning is used in this control.

results.name: Triangle meshes through the same SDF interface
results.summary: Closed triangle meshes now produce distance fields using Warp closest-point and parity queries. A concave-prism check preserves the notch and interior sign. On triangulated box, sphere, and cylinder controls, a 5 mm field changes reconstructed forces by roughly 0.13–0.44 N RMS relative to analytic geometry. Thirty recorded transitions per shape; no MPM solve and no force refitting. Learned dynamics on unseen mesh shapes are not tested.

results.name: Deeper model: large-bed development snapshot
results.summary: An intermediate deeper model still transfers poorly: 2.88 cm particle error, 12.85 cm box-position error, and 80.89 N force error over 0.5 s. This snapshot uses eight message-passing layers, six-frame history, one-step training, and 156 training episodes; the earlier model used three layers, four-step training, and 48 episodes. Several factors differ, so this is not an isolated depth comparison. Larger architecture alone has not established stable deployment.

metrics.scope: Development scaling diagnostic, 100 transitions / 0.5 s; all 296875 particles. Not a full-duration independent test.

results.name: Frozen model through Newton: independent test
results.summary: 12/12 complete 1.5-second test rollouts. Checkpoint and contact parameters were frozen using validation data. Newton handles rigid dynamics; all particle motion comes from the GNN. Partial-rollout errors are shown with their completed length and must not be compared with full-rollout errors.

limitations: The initial model drifted through rigid ground. Longer one-step training alone made this worse.
Static-contact correction is an explicit geometric approximation. Projecting particles against the moving body caused all six coupled validation rollouts to stop early.
Primary training comparisons use free-body rigid integration. A separate Newton MJWarp adapter now handles rigid contacts and completes all six validation episodes.
Material stress and plastic strain are not inputs. Full particle momentum consistency is not enforced.
All three shape families occur in training. Mesh-to-SDF geometry is implemented, but rigid mesh import and learned generalization to unseen mesh shapes remain untested.
The G1-sized bed passes a three-state all-particle inference memory check; stable full-duration rollouts and isolated speed comparisons remain unestablished.
The planned 32-step training extension is validation-only and does not replace the frozen model used for independent test results.
